readout_other: Fluo-4AM calcium imaging of auditory-cortex brain-slice neurons/glia, with pharmacological block of mechanosensitive channels using ruthenium red
direction_notes: Four distinct calcium-response patterns were identified, including both excitatory (influx during stimulation followed by post-stimulus efflux) and inhibitory (efflux during stimulation, in some cases followed by delayed influx) activity across cells.
safety_notes: Directly measured tissue temperature increased by only 0.0062 ± 0.010 °C during the 200-ms stimulation period, indicating negligible thermal effects; acoustic pressure was reported to be well below the cavitation threshold.

exposures.label: Continuous-wave ultrasound stimulation of auditory cortex brain slice

timing.protocol_description: A single 200-ms continuous-wave ultrasound stimulation was delivered per trial, 3 s after the start of fluorescence recording (10 s total per trial); ten trials were conducted per slice with 30-s intertrial intervals. Responses were compared against sham (0 Pa) stimulation trials.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Fig. 8. Feature analysis of $\mathrm { C a } ^ { 2 + }$ dynamics in the pre-US, stim, and post-US windows. A total of 76 cells were analyzed (a: 5 cells, b: 26 cells, c: 18 cells, and d: 27 cells) from 16 slices; $^ { * * * } p < 0 . 0 0 5$ . Dotted lines represent individual cells within each group, and the red line indicates the median. Increases in fluorescence intensity reflect intracellular $\mathrm { C a } ^ { \bar { 2 } + }$ influx, whereas decreases indicate intracellular $\mathrm { C a } ^ { 2 + }$ efflux
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: To quantify cellular activity before and after ultrasound stimulation, slices were loaded with the $\mathrm { C a } ^ { 2 + }$ indicator Fluo-4AM (CS32, Dojindo Laboratories). Ultrasound stimuli consisted of continuous waves at 360 kHz with an acoustic pressure of 92.8 kPa and a duration of 200 ms $( I _ { \mathrm { \ s p p a } } = 2 9 1$ mW/cm<sup>2</sup> in the unit; Fig. 3). The waveform presented in Fig. 3 corresponds to the acoustic pressure signal measured in the experiment. The selection of burst duration was based on the standard transcranial ultrasound stimulation parameters [12], which typically evoke multiple action potentials in single neurons [10]. During each trial, artificial cerebrospinal fluid was perfused through the chamber that was mounted on the PMUT. The fluorescence recording began, and a single ultrasound stimulation was delivered after 3 s; imaging continued for a total of 10 s. Ten trials were conducted with 30-s intertrial intervals. Fluorescence imaging was performed using a fixed-stage upright microscope (BX61WI-35FL/IR7-2, Olympus) equipped with a 40 water-immersion objective lens (LUMPlanFI/IR, Olympus). The emitted fluorescence was captured using a CMOS camera (acA1920-155um, Basler) at a frame rate of 50 fps. Individual cells were identified in the resulting fluorescence images based on their cellular morphology.

flags.reason: 92.8 kPa and 291 mW/cm2 were measured via hydrophone in water/calibration conditions at the stimulation voltage (60 Vpp); the paper does not separately report a pressure value measured with the brain slice in place, so domain is recorded as free-field rather than in-situ.
n_subjects is recorded as the 16 brain slices analysed (from 8 mice); subject_unit is 'preparation' since ultrasound was delivered to slices, not directly to the source animals.
